episodes.title: The SEMA Show has changed over the years…

moments.quote: there's no way that you could tell me that 2018 James Dean would absolutely destroy 2026. James, it's not possible. Yeah. And that's what I think a lot of people look up to James for is that like, he came back and like James is drifting quite a long time now and he's came. He's from, if you were to go back 12, 13 years ago and take a driver who retired and, and say, come back to drifting now. They wouldn't, I personally believe that they would struggle massively, but how much the sport has changed. I think Digo Saito is a great example that like,
moments.why: Gekozen door Joshua op het dashboard

moments.topic: THE TROPHY FLEW HOME IN A DRINKS CABINET
moments.quote: I got to ask about the logistics of bringing that trophy home. Like, did you end up booking a separate seat or like, did you have to keep it on your lap for the whole time or how did that all work out? Yeah, it was quite funny. Actually, the airline that we fly with to California is an Irish airline, Erlingus. Erlingus, yeah. So they're like really supportive, quite cool to, you know, ...
moments.why: Light, funny story about flying the 2026 FD trophy home to Ireland. Easy share.

moments.quote: To bring it home is always quite special. And yeah, I think I'm kind of a guy who like loves the small moments, you know, like it's always nice to come home and, you know, put it on the kitchen table for the first time. And I think when my mom will not take it off the kitchen table for at least probably two months. So that's kind of the rule. If we have a big win, they stay down there. ...
moments.why: Sweet family detail: big wins stay on the kitchen table for two months.

moments.topic: ONE HAND ON THE TITLE, NOT BOTH
moments.quote: Yeah, I'm also a big believer in that it's not over until it's in my hand, you know, and that's kind of yeah, I guess the break between Vegas and Long Beach was quite rough because it's I have one hand on it, but not both. You know, it's very close to being done and but still anything going to happen. I think that's what added so much pressure to the battle. Everyone's like, oh, it's just a top pretty too. But I'm like, yeah, but if I lose this top, or two, Jack or James going to win the event. So I'm not going to be champion.
moments.why: How the pressure felt between Vegas and Long Beach; fans remember that final.

moments.topic: "HE WAS GOING TO BE AN FD CHAMPION"
moments.quote: we all know that here, but I was going to be an FT champion, right? Like, yeah, I think, I think that's a foregone conclusion to be honest. Yeah. So I think like it's in Jerry's point of view, like he worked hard with that kid, the hero worked hard and I felt like he was maybe the last shot was took away from a little bit. So I'm like happy that, you know, you know, hero is such a good ...
moments.why: Conor zegt dat Hiroya Minowa een zekere toekomstige FD-kampioen was voordat hij naar rally ging.

moments.topic: COULD HIROYA MINOWA RACE A US RALLY?
moments.quote: Yeah. Yeah. It's, it's tough to see him step away into rally. And, but at the same time, like it looks like he's doing well there. I have a very strong feeling. We're going to see him climb the ranks of, of rally very soon, which might be very, which could be cool. Cause they're going to have around in the U S next year. So like the chance, there is a chance we might be able to see him ...
moments.why: Speculatie dat Hiroya Minowa volgend jaar een Amerikaanse rallyronde rijdt. Gerucht, gaat naar Joshua.

moments.topic: "YOU DRIVE HOW THE JUDGES TELL YOU"
moments.quote: you know, like, you know, the argument of people saying, Oh, you can't drive how you want to drive in competition. Well, no shit, you know, like, yeah, yeah, exactly. You know, you're going to drive. Yeah, I don't really understand that point. But yeah, of course, like we all critique stuff. We all maybe want stuff to be a little bit different. I think, you know, drifting is involving as a whole when it comes to our rule book and a judging rule book. But I don't get that sometimes, you know, I don't get that point of like, Oh, like, you know, competition driving, you don't drive how you want to drive. But like, that's kind of the whole point, right? Like you go to a room in the morning tree, guys tell you what to do. And you do that job the best you can, and you're going to win the you know, that's kind of my opinion how it works.
moments.why: Strong opinion on the 'you can't drive how you want' debate. Comment bait.

moments.quote: You need real people around you. You don't need people around you that are telling you like, Oh, well you've done good. You know, you lost the battle, but you almost had them. Like that's the part for me. When somebody says to me, I almost had you. I'm like, but you didn't. Yeah. That's the difference. Yeah. Almost had like, I would never, I hate that work being honest. There's one thing what annoys me in drifting when somebody says, Oh, but we almost had you, but you didn't. Yeah. You weren't good enough to have me. So go back and be realistic about that.
moments.why: Blunt quote, very shareable.

moments.topic: HIS SPOTTER WATCHES DRIFT EVENTS IN EGYPT
moments.quote: I said at the banquet, like, I would often text him late at night. And I'm like, what are you doing? He's like, I'm just watching a drift event. And I'm like, where's the drift event? And it's in like Egypt or something. And I'm like, you know, and I love drifting also. And I always felt for a while that I would never meet somebody who loved drifting just as much as me. But I definitely ...
moments.why: Funny detail about how obsessed his spotter Matt is. Name spelling: check.

moments.quote: me and Matt have a very simple number system, what we use. So like in battle situations, like a lot of the time, so Matt will give me a rundown before the battle, what I'm warming the towers up, what to expect, what to approach. But after that, it's very, it's very simple communication. We have a number system that we've studied very to a very high level. You maybe will see me do ...
moments.why: He and his spotter use a number system; slow practice runs are them practising it.

moments.topic: "IF IT FAILS, MY AMERICAN JOURNEY IS OVER"
moments.quote: You know, I talked about a lot about this journey year that in first 15 minutes, I knew that we were going to fight for a championship. That's very true. Like, that's not a saying that I just came up with that actually happened. And it wasn't that the car was that good. I didn't even drive the car at this point. But jury and his team gave me a sense of like, this is where I meant to be ...
moments.why: Strongest story of the episode: all-in bet on Jerry Yang's team.

moments.topic: "JAMES BEATING US WAS THE BEST THING"
moments.quote: we're like, I think we can get back to a good position. Do I think that we can fight for championship? Maybe not. You know, for sure, it wasn't a perfect year. There was still some things what could have been better on my side. And, you know, we had a little bit of bad look. But like, overall, when I look back at the year, I think it was everything what it needed to be. James whooped ...
moments.why: Says losing to James Deane in Orlando turned the season.

moments.topic: HIS CREW CHIEF DOES THE TESTING
moments.quote: Eric, my crew guy, holy shit, he can drive. Like, I actually really want to drive with him. I have watched a lot of these videos and stuff. And like, so anytime the car needed to get tested when I wasn't there, Eric was the one who done the testing on my car as well. Which I thought was sick. Like, there's not many teams can say that their crew chief guy was the guy who was driving it ...
moments.why: Little-known fact: crew chief Eric tests the car when Conor is in Europe.

moments.topic: 1,500 WHP AND NO NOS ALL YEAR
moments.quote: Even in Europe, there was a long time that I used like a smaller turbo than Jack. Right. So the VR suits my style, but then the VR went to the other extreme where we had a problem that it just was too much. Like the engine was too much. Like I was constantly asking to turn it down, turn it down, turn it down, turn it down. To the point that we almost couldn't turn it down anymore. First ...
moments.why: Big numbers and a surprising choice: he asked to turn the engine DOWN.

moments.quote: I was always like, oh, there's a way that we can make run -up better. There has got to be a way to like chasing on the run -up has to be better. So I started left foot braking always on the run -up, on the chase. So I would left foot brake to flick, like mimic the speed. Um, if there, even in Poland and my onboards and stuff, like Dylan Hughes asked me in FD, he was like, that blows my ...
moments.why: Claims he started left-foot braking on the chase run-up and others copied it (mentions Dylan Hughes and LZ). Check names.

moments.quote: There is not much of an off season actually. Um, yeah, I go to Japan next week to do D1, which I'm excited about. Um, yeah, so I got to go there and then I will go to Cyprus, which is kind of like a traditional trip. What Irish drivers do at the end of the year. I haven't went actually in the last three years, so I'm excited to go there. Um, and then I do a rally, which is kind of like ...
moments.why: D1 in Japan, Cyprus, a rally and Oman. Note: recorded right after Long Beach, so 'next week' may be past.

moments.topic: "THE BEST VERSION EVER OF CONOR SHANAHAN"
moments.quote: I really have a goal right now that I probably shouldn't say this, but I really have a goal that I want next year to be the best version ever of Connor Shanahan. And I mean that in many ways, like not just in the car. I mean, like, I really want to spend time working on myself and I want to somewhat take my health more serious towards drifting. I want to try focus more on kind of ...
moments.why: Plans for 2027: more fitness and preparation.

moments.topic: BIG FD CHANGES COMING NEXT YEAR?
moments.quote: Yeah. Yeah. I, next year I'm very, very excited for, I know it looks like there's going to be some changes as well, which is, is kind of cool. I don't know if you got that, the memo about. A lot of changes, I think. Yeah. And I think there's going to be more than even you and I don't have preview too. Like, it's, I know, I'm very excited to see what ends up happening next year with, ...
moments.why: Host and Conor hint at changes for next season they cannot share yet. Rumor, needs Joshua.

moments.quote: And I just want to take this opportunity to say thank you to them as well. And the people who hate me. Thank you so much because you guys motivate me more than ever as well. And keep hating me, please. I don't think there's many, but I'm sure there's some. I'm for sure. I think it's normal when you do something good. Yeah. Yeah. It's a, if somebody's pissed off with where you're going, ...
moments.why: Fun closing line to the haters.

moments.topic: WHY FD IS SO HARD TO WIN
moments.quote: Like no one just becomes a champion without working hard. Like F.D. is probably one of the hardest motorsport championships to win because like you can have the best team in road racing and be a decent driver and keep all four tires on the ground and win a championship road racing. Yeah, it is not like that drifting at all, because you can make a mistake every lap and still win road racing. Yeah, you cannot do that in drifting unless the other guy you're battling does it, too. Yeah. You almost can't make a mistake in a weekend. Like you got to go all the way. And like, you know, usually you make one or two and hopefully the other guy does, too. And then you got to beat the three guys up top that are deciding who wins. Right. Right. Understand what they want. Yeah. Because I'm not fighting for a lap time. Yeah. I'm fighting for a I win or lose.
moments.why: Road racing lets you make mistakes every lap; in drifting one mistake and judges decide.

moments.quote: Like it's like to me, it's very clear. Like I don't think there's to me, there's always a vast difference. Because I think the rules and how F.D. is currently, it doesn't like if you drive the whole track at 50 degrees angle and you fill every zone and then the next guy goes out and does it at 62 degrees angle and fills all the zone, does all the same thing, they're getting the same score. That's what I believe. The problem with F.D. is right now, because the guy with 50 degrees angle did everything great and he did everything he was supposed to. OK. Driving at 62 degrees angle versus 50 is five times harder. Right. Should be that other run should be a 65 and that's a 95.

Or do I just go for what's best and what's the best opportunity for me to build something? Yeah, I mean, it's your money, right? You have to decide what, how it's going to work for you, where you want to put it, because you don't get it back, right?
moments.why: Host reveals his VQ37 build uses GT-R twin turbos and questions sticking to OEM.

moments.topic: COLD AIR INTAKES DON'T MAKE POWER
moments.quote: And, you know, I've seen it firsthand cold air intakes and you know, as well as I do, do not make power. They're not, you know, putting a cold air intake does not necessarily mean that you're going to gain horsepower. You might gain a little bit of feel. It might move the power band around, depending on, you know, flow diameter of the pipe and things like that. Fine. But there's something to be said about a team of engineers that set out to make that, say that manifold, that exhaust manifold flow as efficiently as possible and to work as well as it does into obviously fit. They put a lot of time and effort into the fit and finish and how it's going to fit on the vehicle. And I think that's where we really see that shine through now.
moments.why: Bold claim against a classic first mod, backed by praise for factory engineering.

moments.quote: If not, wiring specialties just recently announced that they're doing a VR 30 swap kit for the Z33 chassis for the 350Z chassis. I think it is brilliant. Like genuinely, I think that it's very smart to keep the longevity of both of the platforms going. Like, yes, the VR 30 has its issues and everyone can complain. And it's gonna and they're getting cheap. You know, let's be honest, the G35 and 350Z have come down significantly. So if you know, for one with a blown engine or anything like that, you can get a chassis. I'm saying for a decent price.

moments.quote: You know, I should say, it sounds like I'm sort of hating on OEM plus built. I'm definitely not. I did one for a little while. And like I said, you know, I got bored and I moved on. A little while. I didn't want a necessity at the time I was very young. And I may or may not have been charged for multiple counts of street racing and whatever. moments.why: Funny confession: multiple street racing charges led to a quiet OEM+ Honda.

moments.quote: That ultimately led, especially in like the Honda and Nissan world, to a lot of theft. And I think it's, you know, it's pretty well known. Type Rs were constantly getting stolen. And you're not going to probably be wanting to drive it once it is making 500 natural, natural aspirated horsepower. It's going to be quite a handful. I'm sure. So my, the thing that I think is that was always just the chase of how to make quick power, how to make it cheap. How to have a fast car. It was never about, hey, I need this part because it makes the car more like the higher trim level. You know, nobody was putting a Hellcat motor in their scat pack to make it a Hellcat. They were just doing it to have a fast scat pack.

moments.quote: That's the same thing with the Volkswagen crowd. And I think even the Corvette crowd too, right? moments.quote: So I know there's a lot, you know, that they have tried. And then unfortunately it's just, this isn't the right recipe. And it's like, this is what we got to use. Um, and it's like, I literally just all year, man, I'm like, I wish we just kind of kept this setup we had in program. I just thought I was a little underpowered. Um, and unfortunately it's just the setup we went with this year. It just didn't give us the sauce we needed.

moments.quote: And it's just like going back to his crew, man. It's just, I remember watching just in Atlanta, the first round, like my crew was there with him and they had, um, impact and went into the wall. And one of my crew guys just looked at me and he goes, we got a lot of work to do just because of how dialed and like things come in. They don't even say anything. Um, and I was definitely humbled by just all of that.

moments.quote: FDs, uh, it's, it's insane how, it's insane how different it is compared to even a pro -am series, right? And we were like, all right, this is where we're going to be. This is what we need. Uh, and we're going to execute and be on that podium.

Like I'm locked into my seat. I have everything, you know, I have my cool suit on. I have my earbuds in like I'm locked in and looking forward.
moments.why: His second kid arrived between rounds two and three of his rookie FD year.

moments.quote: Yeah, I think sleep is number one, but also I work with a sports psychologist. Oh, nice. So having my mindset, but more so keeping me level minded and like saying certain things to myself when I need to say things, then even to practice breathing, like that was something where I was never taught how to properly breathe. And I was like, it sounds so woo woo and dumb, but it is one of the most life -changing things you can learn.
moments.why: He works with a sports psychologist and calls learning to breathe life-changing.

moments.quote: Um, visualizing, like I visualize over and over and over again, the run, I visualize me winning the battle. I visualize the guy pointing to me, you got the win, like that type of stuff. And so when I do get in that position, I feel like I've already been there. And so all the, like I had no nerves whatsoever all year. And like, it's because I mentally prepared myself to be in that position, to be in that seat, especially with the SIM helping out of like literally seeing everything and knowing, okay, this is where I'm going to be.
moments.why: He visualizes winning every battle so he had zero nerves as an FD rookie.

moments.quote: Um, I mean, for us this year, just kind of finishing at the bottom, I think next year, like at a minimum, man, it's like, we have to be a top 10 competitive. Um, of course, like I'm going to tell you, like, we're going to be on the box every single round. Um, but like the realistic goals is just to have a car that is working a hundred percent, um, and just myself being comfortable behind the wheel with all the changes we made this year. Like I felt like I was driving someone else's car for the first three rounds. Like I'm just like, dude, this doesn't feel right. Um, you know, this isn't, this isn't my car. I don't feel comfortable. I'm not going to be able to perform at the level I can.
moments.why: After finishing at the bottom, his minimum goal for next year is top 10.

moments.quote: Uh, I'm just bummed out about how it all kind of panned out, but, uh, yeah, like the one round we, we had essentially like a car, uh, when we made it's top 16 and then, uh, Jerry Johnson took us out and top 16, which was, it was a pretty close battle, but it was a good battle. Everyone was like, Oh, I don't, I didn't know you could drive like that. I'm like, and so I think that's just a really big bummer, man. Like just like people truly think like what we did this year is like the level of my driving, which is like, yeah, embarrassing. Um, you know, but it's just like, again, man, it lights a fire in my butt. Like I cannot wait to get back out there.
moments.why: His one working weekend ended in Top 16 and people finally saw what he can do.

moments.quote: I, I will have my G out there for black Friday. I have a G sedan with the one J in it. And we just, uh, put a four door cage with four bucket seats. Oh, sick. Okay. Yeah. So I really wanted to build a car to like be able to just give ride alongs and, you know, share the experience of drifting. Uh, also give back to the partners that's kind of helped on the build. Um, and so yeah, we're going to be, uh, bringing that car out for black Friday. So super excited about that. And it should be a good time.
moments.why: He built a 1JZ G sedan with a four door cage to give ride-alongs at Black Friday.

moments.quote: And arguably I would put, I would put it like, it's like ProSpec plus. That's like, I don't want to take away anything from ProSpec drivers. Cause I know how much goes into getting you there and like the amount of work that goes into that. But I personally feel like the competition or the level of the competition and the driving in hop it, I think it kind of tips the scale a little bit. You can't, you can't argue with the driver lineup. There's numerous pros in that series. So it's nothing against ProSpec. It is just, this is a series that is full of pros consistently. Like there are some series that have had one pro, maybe two pro you're what six of them or something like that. It's very like every other event is different, but, um, I will say the one thing is like the tracks that we're driving, they're a little bit slower because we're in like smaller speedways, the tire that we're on a little bit less grip than like a prospect tire. So the cars are essentially easier to drive, but still you're going up against really good drivers. So you got to be on top of your game.
moments.why: Ex-FD driver says his grassroots series is tougher than FD ProSpec because it is full of pros.

moments.quote: To be completely honest with you, that's kind of how I'm feeling this year and going into where I kind of want to take drifting for myself is like, now is the time where I've realized like, there's a lot of hard work that I got to put in to be better than just that natural talent. Right. You are a naturally talented driver. But you hit the hard work. I'm at the hard work part. And I think that's some of the reasons why we had so much difficulty in the past. But now looking back at it, stepping back and being able to see what we need to do. Like, I'm actually excited to put in the hard work. And after this year of just getting back in the car, I was like, all right, cool. We got the drive. I'm loving drifting, having a good time. Now I'm going to start packing on the work and start doing it. So I'm hoping next year you'll just see the progression go back up and then we'll be back in maybe a space that we were once before.
moments.why: He admits natural talent was not enough and hints at a return to his old level next year.

moments.topic: HOLE IN THE MOTOR AT LAGUNA SECA
moments.quote: There's a hole in my motor. Yeah. But, but you know, having the willpower to just laugh it off. Yeah. It took me a little bit. Cole Richards was like next to me. I had no idea that my, my motor was blown up. They pushed me down the corkscrew and I made it like rolled all the way into the pits. And Cole was like, what happened? I was like, dude, made the craziest noise. Was idling like crazy. Dude, this car is idling for a little bit. That's crazy. It was zero oil pressure. But, um, yeah, he saw it and he was like, oh, there's a hole in it. And I was like, it took me a little bit to like be able to laugh. I was like, I kind of want to cry about this right now, dude. It's just, I was just so excited to drive this event, but it's, it's fine. We're all fine now.
moments.why: His engine blew at Gridlife Laguna; Cole Richards spotted the hole as he rolled down the Corkscrew.

moments.topic: WHY HE WAS REMOVED FROM FD
moments.quote: But the one thing that I really don't want to do is I do not want to miss the last round of a hot pit. I was just talking to Jacob. He was like, hey, I know it's kind of a sore subject right now, but like, you want to be there? What do you want to do? And I was like, I don't know what I can do, but all I know is I don't want to miss the last round because that's like something remembering FD is something that like eats away me the most. So it's like watching it. Yeah. So the season, the world, the season, the last season I drove with FD was also the reason why I was removed from FD because I didn't make all the rounds and like that killed me inside because they like I felt like they didn't know how much I wanted to be there and I couldn't. Like I hated the idea of people seeing it as, oh, he's just like stressed out and he's going through shit. So he's just staying home. It's like, no, I want to be there so bad. I couldn't make it happen. Yeah, that's like a bad memory for me. So this year I wanted to just be like, all right, we made every round. We competed all year.
moments.why: He reveals missing rounds in his last FD season is why he lost his spot, and how much that still hurts.

moments.quote: I got I got called out a while ago. Someone's like, dude, talks about like supporting local. He doesn't even work for, you know, US drift circuit. Oh, so which which is a very valid point. And at first I was like, I was like, screw you, dude. And I thought about it like, no, but that's right. But then I called Chris Jackson. I was like, hey, can I do commentaries? I thought you would never ask. So now I'm doing a program series. It's like, OK, there you go.
moments.why: The FD commentator got called out for not supporting his local series, so he phoned them and got a job.

moments.topic: FOUR ENGINES IN ONE ROOKIE SEASON
moments.quote: But yeah, we've gone through four motors this year. I didn't even realize that. Pretty quiet about it. Yeah. Long Beach was good. Atlanta, we had a motor issue. Orlando and then Connecticut, we put like the spare of the spare motor in. It was like, oh, that thing's not great. Do you know why they're letting go? The one from Orlando was just a manufacturing issue. Okay. Push rod. Oh, weird. And the other two were just like worn out. They were fresh rebuilds, but they just got worn out.
moments.why: An FD rookie reveals he has gone through four engines this season, and why they failed.

moments.topic: NEW CHASSIS AND STROKER 2JZ FOR NEXT YEAR
moments.quote: Next year, same. Well, different chassis, but same platform. So do you already have the new chassis? Yeah. So it's still the FRS chassis, but it's a gen two body kit. It's your inner body kit. Oh, cool. And then three, two, two J built by J and Maher. Maher, I don't know his last name. RS garage. Yes. And then working with Freddie with a pretty good engine package. Have a little bit more power. That's a good combo. Yeah. That's a good deal. They got sauce over there. Stroker two J. Yeah. Yeah. I feel like we fixed the stroker issue in drifting. There was a minute where strokers were not working out too well. A lot of blown engines. Yeah. And it's cool seeing like Freddie and J kind of R &D some things and then find out what works and what doesn't work. And Adam goes out and tests them. And he just rips out of the box. Thanks Adam for being the test meal for the rest of us. Appreciate that buddy.
moments.why: An FD rookie reveals his next-year car: new FR-S chassis, gen two body kit and a stroker 2JZ.

moments.quote: Well, funny story. We were at Adams with, there was a gang of FD drivers there right before Orlando. And we were there. Freddie was dinoing the FRS and Jack and Connor were there and they pulled up my video talking to Freddie and he's like, he just needs a Jay Z already. Look at how he's driving in Atlanta. Well, you get the Jay Z. You paddle dance a lot, right? Yeah. Like you are, you drive it like a two -stroke. Right. There's a few drivers that, that kind of do that. The Shannon hands do it like Connor's foot games is James. Yeah. James drives a V8. Like it's a 2J.
moments.why: Jack and Conor Shanahan watched his Atlanta footage and told him he needs a 2JZ.

moments.quote: So I think what it is is that like, when I started driving up in Southern Oregon, when I was a wee lad, um, we were just drifting at the, the, um, the fairgrounds there at a, in a skid pad. And then the first road course that I ever went to was a thunderhill. Have you ever been there? And that front straight, they hadn't even built West yet. Uh, and that front straight away. And then that huge left -hander uphill with like, like 10 miles of run out, you could leave the property and still be just fine. But, uh, yeah, we were doing, um, like 120, 130 mile an hour entries when I was like 17, 18. So I think it's just a, uh, like a comfort thing. It's just like, I've been doing it for so long that like all the high -speed stuff is, it's just like, that was the first stuff that I start because you have to drive fast at thunderhill to be able to make it.
moments.why: Matt Field explains his Laguna speed: as a teen he did 120 to 130 mph entries at Thunderhill.

moments.topic: WHY HIS FD CAR GOT WALKED
moments.quote: And my car, since it's a pickup truck, like, um, it was the same one that I ran an FD. I've been driving this car for 11 years. Um, there's no rear weight. It's like, you have a battery back there in an oil tank. I'm still front rad. I'm still front everything. And I was like that. So that's why at FD, if it was a momentum bleeding track, so it's like at evergreen where you got all your momentum at the beginning, held it, and then slowed down the rest of the course, the car was fine. But then at any sort of place where I had to dig, I would just up in the land, like road Atlanta, coming up the hill or anything that came out of something slow into like gaining speed. People would just walk me. You couldn't put the weight down. Yeah. But I'm a, I'm a big like proponent of like everything happens for a reason. And so it's like, and I never was like stoked about that the way that that car drove, um, for FD. Uh, but once again, if the car had been developed correctly and like, was a good, like a winning car for FD, it wouldn't have been good for doing this stuff.
moments.why: Matt Field explains why his front-heavy car struggled in FD but is perfect for high speed.

moments.quote: Like the first year when I came to Laguna, I had the idea I was just because I'd been doing a bunch of high speed stuff since I was a little kid. Um, I was like, Oh, I want to link up and over the crest all the way down to turn one, and I, I mentioned it to like a couple other FD drivers and they're like, that's impossible. You can't do that. And it is a very long run. And because in their used to in their mind, thinking of such a gripped up car that's going to drive in and to them it is difficult, but for my car is like perfect. So for me, yeah, I don't know. It was, it was like 10 years or six years of formula D struggling in a car that wasn't so good, but being able to allow me to come here and do this and like positively changed my life for forever.
moments.why: Other FD drivers told Matt Field linking over the Laguna crest was impossible; then he did it.

moments.quote: What's, what's funny is maybe not funny, but like with the new, I don't know how much F D stuff you keep up on, but like the way the judging has developed over say last two years guys like you and forest would probably do so much better now with the current judging standard elaborate on that. Well, so Reese, Reese, Aaron, I own spotter. Exactly. Now one of the judges and, and you know, so he's, he's taken that East coast big swinging, you know, stylish set up and really pushed it. Robbie Nishida, obviously he's, he's judging as well as Vernon. Vernon comes from European drifting, which is much more style based as opposed to speed based. Brian is still there, but Brian of the American judges was the most style based. So you're talking about two East coast guys, a Japanese guy and a European guy, those are your judges. So the way that they have been waiting things is much more, if the lead screws up, it's an impossible chase. Whereas I feel like let's go back 10 years. It was like, no, chase, you have to adapt to the lead. That isn't really the case anymore.
moments.why: The host argues current FD judging would suit stylish drivers like Matt Field and Forrest Wang.

moments.quote: I, I, I put it like this, like with formula, you know, in life, we all walk through hallways and pass by doors, different choices that you can make different things than for a lot of us that dream about formula drift and whatnot. Like it was coming across a golden door, like in crested wood jewels and seeing like golden light come from underneath it. And it's like, and I stood there like forever trying to like force this door open and then, and I even said like, when I was on the road, like to St. Louis that year that I broke my arm, I was like, if I'm not supposed to be here, show me, and then like, and then I broke my arm. And I consider that to be the greatest blessing ever. And it wasn't until I stepped away from the golden door that I, I thought that it was because it was before me and I could grab the handle like it was, it had to be for me, right? But then it wasn't until I stood against the door, like stood against the wall and then like gave up and I stopped driving for two years, then all of a sudden a little, a little dusty door beside me pops open and I'm like, oh, what's behind here? And behind that was all the most important people in my life, people that believed in me and supported me. And they were the ones that got me to go to form to Laguna here the very first time. And that completely all the greatest things that beyond my wildest dreams that I ever could have, I don't know, conjured were behind that, that dusty door.
moments.why: Matt Field on chasing FD like a golden door, and how breaking his arm became a blessing.

moments.topic: WOULD MATT FIELD RETURN TO FD?
moments.quote: So, and but you continue to walk through hallways and you continue to like be presented with life choices. And so I'm sure that if there was a day where all of a sudden another little dusty door pops open, like in that offers me the opportunity to go back to empty, I would take it. Yeah. Yeah. But I just going to force the door. Exactly. Like, yeah, life isn't about forcing things. It's about, you know, dealing with circumstances and making the best of it. And so one day I would love to. I would. But I just need the right people. I need the right team. I need a car that I like. I actually like have a say in and like can be built at a proper manner for today's sport and just. Yeah, I would love to. I just it's got to work.
moments.why: Matt Field says he would take an FD return, but only with the right team and car.

moments.quote: If if FD or high level drifting in general is not first or second, it is nothing. You're last. Exactly. Exactly. And sometimes even being first is not enough. Yeah, it's tough. It's it and people don't understand. It's like, oh, yeah, I stress about things too. It's like, no, you literally like from the moment that I would be going to bed, I would have these I would harbor these anxieties around the team or around like the car or the things that people are saying online budget, just the support everything. And then all of a sudden, like and then I would go to sleep, have like sleeping and like having dreams was the only escape. And then like you would wake up and I would instantly start stressing about it.
moments.why: If FD is not first or second in your life it is nothing; Matt describes the constant anxiety.

moments.quote: Like from top to bottom, it was it was that was that was a weird, difficult part, though, as well. Is because people in the industry that I had had high regards for respect for that wouldn't necessarily give me the time of day before they would kind of like brush me off, they'd be like, oh, Matt, like, yeah, whatever. They're going to see all of a sudden, like when that stupid first video happens and like ESPN posts like went all over the place. Then like all of a sudden, people that had never given me the time a day where all of a sudden pat me on the back.
moments.why: People who brushed Matt Field off suddenly patted him on the back after his viral video.

moments.topic: WORLD CLASS ON A GRASSROOTS BUDGET
moments.quote: I I'm very happy. I feel very blessed. Like I went from like a formula D like your it's so expensive. And I'm paying like six dudes like getting their flights, hotels and all that sort of stuff. I showed up at this event with just myself and my girlfriend. Like there's like we there's no crew. And like I'm just buying tires and like getting fuel and like all that sort of stuff. So it's like it's I'm like spending a grassroots budget. And but getting to do like world class stuff, it's it's so fun. Yeah, it's a blessing. I'm so lucky.
moments.why: From paying six crew in FD to showing up with just his girlfriend.

moments.quote: But my dad was into like he he loved old war birds. And we grew up like where I live in Southern Oregon is a big retirement community. So there's a bunch of people with like random war birds in there. And that's where like this machine, the aviation theming from Mars. Yeah, that's where that came from. And so and so he went down in a T -28, which is a World War Two trainer. And they're they're pretty quick bird and they don't glide very well. So and then he he lost the oil system above the Black Rock Hills in Northern California. When went to the ground, his buddy that was in the plane passed away. He was in a coma for six months. She said, but then and then he passed away before I was 18. And so he really liked the hot rods like that sort of stuff. I'm I'm like a member of the like I learned all of my driving in the mountains in his Dodge Ram, like when he when he got his accident, couldn't drive anymore. So I got my driver's license, drove his Dodge Ram.
moments.why: Matt Field explains his aviation theme comes from his late father, who crashed a T-28 warbird.

moments.quote: Like I quit drifting for two full years. And I drove in the mountains every single night. But I was like this sport. I was like, it soured me entirely for my passion. And then when I finally when I got an opportunity to drive drift week and I built a C6, right? Through a set of knuckles on in the handbrake. When did drift week and met all my best friend, like the people that I love the most in this world. And then like, oh, where was I going with that? It was it. I literally got out of the car at Villain Sports Land because I had been lying to myself. I was like, I don't belong here. This sport obviously has rejected me like I don't. This is not my sport. And then when I finally went to Villain Sports Land and drifted again for the first time in like two years, like properly drifted. Then I like went back to my pits. I like just got in my car. Everybody's like, how was it? I was like, good. And I just walked off into the field like into the sunset. Just here, bawling. Because you know, yeah, I knew I was like, I do love this. And I am passionate about this.
moments.why: After quitting for two years, Matt Field drifted again and walked off into the field in tears.

episodes.title: The Best & Worst factory wheels… “WHY ARE THE WHEELS SQUARE?!”

moments.topic: MATT FIELD ON HIS VEGAS LAYOUT
moments.quote: This is how I feel about the track. If the transition from bank to flat was like 10 % better, it would be an amazing, like perfect track. And whether the layout that me and Ryan and Ken chose for the infield was optimal, sure, surely not, right? We could sit here and say, this corner could be this, and this corner could be that. But here's the beautiful thing, we have a contract for a couple years, and the plan is to come back and continue to make it better. By no means, I hope that we do the exact same layout just because there was a successful weekend. There's better stuff out there, so. Let's explore, let's do stuff, and the coolest thing is that the track is all about us and us being here, and I think we put it on an amazing show for the fans, and this is what's most important, not whether we think the track is good, it's whether the fans think the tandem was good, and that's kind of the end of the day.
moments.why: Matt Field reveals he co-designed the Vegas layout, the deal runs a couple of years and the track will change.

moments.guest: JACK SHANAHAN, MATT FIELD, CONOR SHANAHAN
moments.quote: I mean, more than the car. Like it looked like, in general, the whole grid was kind of struggling with temps today. I think, to be honest, it was like the lack of air moving into place at the issue. Like my car, we went through everything, and everything was actually still as good as it has been all season. But even driving around between the lead and the chase, or chase and the lead. Don't cool off. It didn't cool off. I was like, you actually had to go real fast. And like idle for it to work. So it was weird. It was just very, very still air. Drift cars are funny, where they don't do anything other than drift, even unless you're sitting still. Then they do car things. Other than that, they do terrible. It's like the first event that I feel like we couldn't even do donuts, because I finished the second run, and I was like, oh my God, this thing is on X Games mode on the back. I was turning my fan on early. I never touch buttons. Yeah, I never, yeah. My car in the final was hot.
moments.why: The podium explains how still desert air had cars overheating all night, even between runs.

moments.guest: JACK SHANAHAN, MATT FIELD, CONOR SHANAHAN
moments.topic: HOW PRO DRIFT CARS STAY COOL
moments.quote: Yeah, yeah, we brought the fans in 10 degrees earlier, just to try to help with the split between two runs, let's say. Do you, question that, now that you mentioned that, do you guys not run fans during the actual run itself, or only if we hit 200, we're bringing them in? Oh no, fans run nearly all the time. We just did a thing. Yeah, the computer was that. We got a computer for that. Yeah, we come on at a certain temperature, basically. When the car reaches a certain temperature, the fans come on.
moments.why: A quick look at how teams run cooling fans in a Pro drift car.

moments.topic: JACK'S CAR: JUST TIRES AND FUEL
moments.quote: I want to go to sleep, to be honest. But other than that, not really. I think we're sitting forward, but much closer to second now than we have been, so that's cool. You're like one battle up and you're in second, basically. Oh yeah, well, sweet, we can do that, you know? So, yeah, no, to be honest, if we can finish one, two in the championship, the first time we've done an approach championship since, I think we've done it in BDC. I think it's 2017. It's quite cool, you know what I mean? So if we can finish that strong, I wouldn't be mad at all. That would be fairly fucking cool, to be honest. So, yeah, no, my second year here, and with relatively small program, like low budgets and building the car in such a short time, I'm more than happy, to be honest, with what we've done. The guys are good. Corey's great. Everything has just been working fairly flawlessly, to be honest. Since Long Beach, we had the issues, but since Long Beach, the car has literally had nothing but tires and fuel. It's fairly impressive. So I'm very, very proud of that. It's been quarter panels, tires and fuel.
moments.why: Jack Shanahan on chasing a Shanahan one-two in the title with a low budget car that has needed nothing since Long Beach.

moments.quote: I think the pressure is the fun part, though. Like, pressure to have fun? Or like, you enjoy the pressure? No, when the pressure's there, it's more fun. Got it. I'm having less fun. I've said it, like, walking up and down the grid, you guys have probably heard me, I'm like, I'm bored. You want the stress? Yeah. Yeah. Like, OK, somebody crashes out on track. I'm like, I'm so bored now. Like, I was amped, and I'm in it, and I'm ready to do it, and I'm checking boxes, and we're coming in swinging. And then now it's like, all right, just hang out for another two hours. I'm like, I'm bored. But when there's a championship fight, you're like, all right, I got to get into my head space. I got to do this. I got to do this. You're thinking about this. You're thinking about that. It's just more fun to be in it. Gotcha. I don't know. I'm bored, but at the same time, I'm absolutely thankful that I'm able to be bored, but still compete for wins and still be able to throw down. So that's just a testament to the series and the team.
moments.why: Out of the title fight, Matt Field says racing without championship pressure is less fun.

moments.quote: I just got to prepare for Long Beach the same as I prepare for every other race. Like I want to go there and try when they event. That's the goal. Yeah. You know, I kind of said started this weekend, I was asking me about points and this. And I'm like, I'm going to drive hard, try when they event. And we'll look at the points that night and see what we need to do. But I'm really happy in the position that I'm in. Like, you know, we won a long beach, which was like a dream start. And it kind of almost was like too good of a start, because it made us a little bit like and then we had a mechanical in Atlanta. And then I thought it was a great idea to battle James in top 32 in Orlando. And he woke my ass. So I was kind of like, damn, this is like a mechanical atop 32 and I kind of made the year a little bit stressful after a really good start. Then we got back in the podium in Connecticut and yeah, just kind of believe that we can get back in the fight, worked hard. And the boys all worked hard around me. I think when we had the mechanical Atlanta and then we had the top 32 in Orlando, it was kind of like, OK, this is going to be like a foundation year for next year to fight for a championship.
moments.why: Conor Shanahan looks back on a season with a dream start, a mechanical and a lesson from James Deane.

moments.quote: You know, I got to give such props to the guys. They're doing such a good job. Like this weekend, I came done practice for qualifying, qualified really strong. The only change we made to the car is one PSI from the start to the weekend. Yeah, Jackson, not even a shock change. Nothing. OK. And it's like for me, the car is just giving everything I want. I feel no pressure driving the car. It's easy to do good lead runs. It's it's just a really good, happy environment for me to be in. So it kind of makes my driving a lot more fun and I'm enjoying that. And I guess I've had experience with that at the other side of the world.
moments.why: Conor Shanahan says the only setup change all weekend was one PSI of tire pressure.

moments.quote: And yeah, look, of course, I want to be champion. That was the goal at the start of the year. That was the goal coming to Long Beach. There's no point saying it wasn't. If you're not showing up trying to be a champion, there's no point coming to the racetrack. So of course, we're in a good position now, but it's drifting. It's not over until it's over. And yeah, we just got to keep working hard. I'm not going to get lazy. The team is not going to get lazy. They're going to do everything on their side to check everything, what they need to check to make sure that they give me the car in Long Beach. And yeah, fingers crossed I can try to get the job doing and be it's my dream. It's the dream of 12 year old Connor sitting at home in the couch watching Formula Drift and yeah, be pretty special moment if it happens.
